title: Chilaquiles Verde Bake
subtitle: Tortilla chips baked in green salsa with eggs, crema, and cotija.
description: Tortilla chips baked in green salsa with eggs and cheese — Mexican breakfast casserole style that feeds ten from one pan.

ingredients.name: cotija cheese
ingredients.notes: crumbled, plus cilantro and radish slices

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chilaquiles Verde Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Roast and blend salsa
steps.instruction: Roast tomatillos, onion, and jalapeños on a sheet pan at 425°F until charred in spots, about 12 minutes. Blend with broth until smooth, then simmer in a pot 10 minutes until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep hotel pan or two 9x13 dishes. Warm salsa off heat—you want it hot but not boiling when it hits the chips.

steps.title: Toss chips with salsa
steps.instruction: Toss chips with just enough warm salsa to coat—about two-thirds of the batch. Reserve remaining salsa for serving. Chips should look sauced but not swimming or they will turn to mush.

steps.title: Bake and add eggs
steps.instruction: Spread chips in the pan and bake 8 minutes. Make ten wells, crack an egg into each, and bake 10–12 more minutes until whites are set (165°F) and yolks are jammy.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Chilaquiles Verde Bake onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Finish and portion
steps.instruction: Drizzle crema in zigzags, scatter cotija and cilantro, and serve with reserved warm salsa and lime wedges. Portion with a wide spatula to keep layers intact.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Chilaquiles Verde Bake — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Use thick chips only—thin restaurant chips dissolve before eggs finish baking.
Hold extra salsa warm for crew members who want a saucier plate at the line.
Cut radishes and cilantro while the first bake runs so garnish is ready at the oven door.
cleanupNotes: Soak the hotel pan immediately with hot water—baked salsa and cheese glue sets fast.
Rinse the blender with warm water before tomatillo skins dry inside the jar.
leftovers: Chilaquiles soften overnight; re-crisp on a sheet pan at 375°F for 8 minutes before reheating.
Fold leftovers into breakfast burritos with scrambled eggs and extra hot salsa.
